instruction.text: Put the sequence of how sound is made into the correct order.

atoms.text: The air around the object vibrates.
The vibrations travel through the air.

instruction.text: Our ears act like funnels. The outer ear catches the sound and directs it into the ear canal. Find the opening of the ear canal in the image.
Drag the vibrations into the ear canal.

atoms.b: Sound is funnelled into the ear ((++canal river)). It hits the ear drum, making it ((++vibrate pop)). These vibrations are then turned into signals that are sent to the ((++brain feet)).

instruction.text: Our ears are very sensitive and can be damaged by loud noises. Select all the things we can do to protect our ears in loud environments.

b: get closer to the source of the sound
++move further away from the source of the sound

instruction.text: Would you need ear protection to stand next to these things? Drag the images to the correct group.

trainers.hint: Select each image to hear the sound it makes.

feedback.finish: For most sounds in our everyday lives, we don’t need to protect our ears; however, we should use ear protection if a sound is really loud and we have to listen to it for a long time.
